items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy 'what if' geography Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how cool this story is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement ('WOW' energy), build excitement through each line, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. 'Plot twist' gets a playful, knowing, excited lift. Each game place ('Vice City?', 'Grassrivers?') is asked like a quick quiz, then answered with delight. 'But that's not even the weirdest part' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. 'A hill...' and 'Nope... Tallahassee' are deadpan and funny. The last line trails off unfinished on 'Because honestly...', voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Say GTA as the letters G-T-A. Pronounce 'Leonida' as 'lee-oh-NEE-dah', 'Kalaga' as 'kah-LAH-gah', 'Gellhorn' as 'GEL-horn', 'Tallahassee' as 'tal-uh-HASS-ee'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word, every line in order; never add words of your own.
lines: What if G-T-A six's Leonida... was a real state?
Plot twist: it already is. It's Florida.
The Leonida Keys... the Florida Keys.
Grassrivers? The Everglades... nicknamed the River of Grass.
And Port Gellhorn sits up on the Panhandle.
So what would this state get?
Over twenty-three million people... the third biggest state in America.
And the longest coastline in the lower forty-eight.
But here's the catch: the game map is tiny.
Fans measured it: about the size of the city of Miami.
Real Florida? Over a thousand times bigger.
But that's not even the weirdest part.
Leonida has a mountain: Mount Kalaga.
Florida's highest point? A hill... a hundred and five meters.
The lowest high point of any U.S. state.
Then there's the capital. Vice City? Nope... Tallahassee.
And Florida has just one thing to say.
So... Leonida, or Florida? Because honestly...
